tools.name: search
tools.description: Search every public page of the Bluebird Technologies website (services, case studies, about, FAQ, contact). Returns page ids for fetch.

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Return one page of the website as Markdown. Pass an id from search or list_pages (e.g. "/work/raubex"), or the page URL.

tools.name: list_pages
tools.description: Every public page with its summary, optionally of one kind: home, work, projects, about, jobs, partners, contact, checklist, quote-calculator, legal, service, case-study. Case studies are kind "case-study"; the engagement types are kind "service".

tools.name: get_contact
tools.description: How to start a conversation with Bluebird Technologies: the email address and a link to the enquiry form with a topic chosen (software, ai, readiness, roadmap, venture, za, partners, other). It sends nothing; the user submits the form themselves.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: fetch, get_contact · Private data: search, list_pages, get_contact · Public sink: get_contact.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: fetch, get_contact · Private data: search, list_pages, get_contact · Public sink: get_contact

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
